Pulse

Reviewer guide

Getting started as a Reviewer

Three steps from a shared folder to your first completed review cycle — getting Pulse running on your machine, picking the Reviewer role, and running a review from start to finish.

1. Run Pulse locally 2. Choose Reviewer 3. Start a review Quick reference Troubleshooting

Before you start

  • Chrome or Edge. Pulse's folder-sync only works in these two browsers — Safari and Firefox can open the app, but can't link the shared folder.
  • A copy of the Pulse folder, or access to the shared folder your team already syncs it through.
  • A password, only if your Admin protected the Reviewer role with one. Pulse will ask if it applies to you.
1

Get Pulse running on your machine

Pulse is a single app folder — no install, no account. You need the whole folder, not just one file.

Put it anywhere on your own machine — Desktop or Documents is fine.

Open the folder and double-click pulse.html. It opens straight in your browser — that's it.

2

Choose the Reviewer role

The first time Pulse opens on a machine, it shows a role picker before anything else.

This isn't a login — it's a soft, on-device switch that decides what you can edit. It doesn't add real security (anyone with access to the file can see everything, regardless of role) — think of it as a workflow safety rail, not a lock.

  1. In the tile grid, click Reviewer.
  2. If your Admin set a password for the role, enter it when asked. Don't have it? Ask your Admin.
  3. Click Done.

Right after, Pulse asks you to link a folder — mandatory for every role, since it's how your work gets saved and shared with your team.

Pick carefully Choosing a different or empty folder is the most common way to end up staring at a board with none of your team's data on it. If you're not sure which folder is the right one, ask before linking.

You can switch roles again any time from the shield icon in the top-right of the toolbar — no need to reopen the app.

3

Start a review cycle

  1. In the left sidebar, click the workstream you want to review — not "All Workstreams," since a review is always scoped to one at a time.
  2. Click Review in the top navigation.
  3. Make sure you're on the Review sub-tab (it reads Review Status if a real workstream isn't selected yet).
  4. Click Start review cycle.

Starting a cycle opens the live checklist — every scope item in the workstream, with its milestones underneath.

For each item, click the small circle on its row to confirm it — confirming an item with several milestones confirms all of them at once; click again to un-confirm. Anything already marked Complete is treated as confirmed automatically, so you're only reviewing what's still open.

Click the chevron on an item's row to expand it, and you'll see its milestones — one row each, with their own Due date, Actual date, and Status.

This is where a Reviewer can correct things directly, without switching back to Planning:

  • Click a milestone's Status badge to cycle it — Not Started → On Track → At Risk → Off Track → Completed.
  • Click a milestone's Due date to edit it directly, or the small + under Actual to record when it actually happened.

You can correct an item's IT/Business/Budget tags the same way, right from its own row in the checklist.

Once every item is confirmed, Complete review lights up.

Click it to close out the cycle. Started a review by mistake instead? Cancel review removes it entirely — no history kept, so use Complete if there's anything worth recording.

Once you've wrapped up, you can attach meeting minutes to the cycle from its row in History (the small document icon) — paste in notes from your review meeting and Pulse will try to auto-split them into a summary, decisions, next steps, and action items.

Quick reference

A few other things worth knowing

Things that'll make more sense once you've run your first cycle, but are worth knowing going in.

Sidebar status badges

In review Overdue

Amber while a cycle's active, red once a workstream has gone stale — or was never reviewed at all.

More than one checklist

Review mode also has Action Log, Decision Log, and Change Log sub-tabs — running records of what got tracked and changed, per workstream or across all of them.

What Reviewer can't do

Restructuring the plan itself — adding or removing workstreams, scope items, or milestones — is one tier up, at Editor. Flag it to whoever holds that role instead.

If something's not working

Troubleshooting

?I don't have the Reviewer password.

Ask whoever set it up — your Admin. Pulse has no way to recover or bypass it for you.

?The board looks empty, or shows the wrong programme.

You most likely linked a different folder than the one your team actually uses. Reopen the folder-sync indicator in the topbar, unlink, and relink to the correct shared folder.

?"Choose a folder" isn't doing anything.

Make sure you're using Chrome or Edge — folder syncing isn't available in Safari or Firefox.

Pulse — Reviewer guide Local-first. Nothing here ever leaves your machine except through the folder you choose.
